recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. If the Python library entries or implementation-type organization need updates, maintain them on the Confluence Open Source Implementations page rather than in the FHIR core source checkout.
issue_request: FHIR-30088 was Published with a Persuasive with Modification resolution for R5. It asked to add fhir.resources and fhir-py to the Python Reference Implementations section on the downloads page, with the accepted modification moving reference implementation/library listings to the HL7 Confluence Open Source Implementations page and organizing them there by language and implementation type.
initial_application: Jira cites Lloyd McKenzie's commit f575ef6b27e6bc5fc01db942c9cf8d00f50099f2, which replaced the local downloads-page Reference Implementations rows, including Python entries, with a Confluence Open Source Implementations link. Zulip discussion shows FHIR-30088 arose from the Python stream and that Ilya Beda updated the Confluence page. Later FHIR-31735 commits 472abf78c495c2ae44924d499be7434ed50788d0 and e404ccd07129409bf907b904ae62ded6c82d28bf moved additional mutable tools, server, and library lists out of core pages and into Confluence-backed registries.
additional_context: source/downloads.html and source/implsupport-module.html are active build pages per source/hierarchy.xml and publish.ini. The current downloads page links implementation tooling to the FHIR Tools Registry, while the Implementation Support module links developers to the Open Source Implementations page. Existing combined-branch audits for FHIR-31735, FHIR-31741, and FHIR-33980 already record this same Confluence-handoff pattern for mutable tools and SDK/library listings.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current source already implements the accepted direction by avoiding per-language Python/library rows in core and pointing implementers to maintained Confluence pages.
